question: Can defects in speakers or texts undermine their own authority?
premises: The listed defects can uproot the authority of the sages' own speech.
Even in the Veda, what is said not to be eaten is elsewhere taught as edible.
Such reversals weaken claims to simple, uniform authority.
inference: Authority cannot rest on bare citation when the cited sources contain self-undermining contradictions.
uncertainties: The verse does not specify which Vedic passages are in view.
plain_english: These defects can uproot the authority of the sages' own words; even in the Veda, what is said not to be eaten is taught elsewhere as something to be eaten.
